import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Reed's omega, delta, and chi conjecture

*References*:
- [B. Reed,  ω Δ and χ, J. Graph Theory 27 (1998) 177-212.](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/(SICI)1097-0118(199804)27:4%3C177::AID-JGT1%3E3.0.CO;2-K)
- [openproblemgarden](http://www.openproblemgarden.org/op/reeds_omega_delta_and_chi_conjecture)
- [mathoverflow/37923](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/37923) asked by user [Andrew D. King](https://mathoverflow.net/users/4580/andrew-d-king)
-/

open scoped Finset

namespace ReedOmegaDeltaChi

/--
For a graph $G$, we define $\Delta(G)$ to be the maximum degree, $\omega(G)$ to be the size of the
largest clique subgraph, and $\chi(G)$ to be the chromatic number. Reed's omega, delta, and chi
conjecture states that $$\chi(G) \leq \lceil \frac{1}{2}(\omega(G) + \Delta(G) + 1) \rceil.$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem reed_omega_delta_chi_conjecture :
  ∀ {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V),
    let χ := G.chromaticNumber
    let ω := G.ecliqueNum
    let Δ := G.emaxDegree
    2 * χ ≤ ω + Δ + 2 := by
  sorry

/--
For a finite graph $G$, we define $\Delta(G)$ to be the maximum degree, $\omega(G)$ to be the
size of the largest clique subgraph, and $\chi(G)$ to be the chromatic number. Reed's omega,
delta, and chi conjecture states that $$\chi(G) \leq \lceil \frac{1}{2}(\omega(G) + \Delta(G) + 1) \rceil.$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem reed_omega_delta_chi_conjecture_for_finite_graphs :
  ∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
    let χ := G.chromaticNumber
    let ω := G.cliqueNum
    let Δ := G.maxDegree
    2 * χ ≤ ω + Δ + 2 := by
  sorry

/--
The simplest open case is when $\Delta(G) = 6$ and $\omega(G) = 2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem reed_conjecture_Δ_6_ω_2 :
  ∀ {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V), G.emaxDegree = 6 ∧ G.cliqueNum = 2 → G.chromaticNumber ≤ 5 := by
    sorry

end ReedOmegaDeltaChi

reformulations.difference: Allows arbitrary, possibly infinite graphs and uses extended-natural invariants, rather than restricting to finite graphs with ordinary integer invariants.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: On finite graphs, ecliqueNum and emaxDegree equal the natural clique number and maximum degree, cast to ℕ∞. If either extended invariant is ⊤, the displayed inequality holds automatically. Otherwise write them as w,d ∈ ℕ. The finite conjecture makes every finite subgraph colorable with floor((w+d+2)/2) colors, since its clique number and maximum degree are at most w,d. Finite-color compactness then colors the entire graph with that many colors. Conversely, specialize the general statement to finite graphs. Together with the ceiling identity, this proves equivalence to the source's finite conjecture. Proved as ReedReview.general_iff_source in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean.

reformulations.difference: Replaces χ ≤ ceil((ω+Δ+1)/2) with 2*χ ≤ ω+Δ+2, using ℕ∞ arithmetic and casts of the natural-valued invariants.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For natural w,d, ceil((w+d+1)/2) = floor((w+d+2)/2). Hence an integer c satisfies the ceiling bound exactly when 2*c ≤ w+d+2. The equivalence also holds for c = ⊤ in ℕ∞, because both inequalities then fail against the finite bound. Proved directly for each finite graph and universally as ReedReview.finite_iff_source in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean.

reformulations.difference: Uses exact hypotheses emaxDegree = 6 and cliqueNum = 2, whereas MathOverflow highlights triangle-free graphs with maximum degree at most six; Lean also allows infinite graphs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For any graph, cliqueNum = 2 is equivalent to ecliqueNum = 2: the natural supremum's unbounded-case default is zero, so it cannot satisfy this hypothesis. Triangle-freeness is equivalent to ecliqueNum ≤ 2. Given any triangle-free graph with maximum degree ≤ 6, adjoining a disjoint K₁,₆ produces a graph with maximum degree exactly six and clique number exactly two. A 5-coloring of the enlarged graph restricts to the original graph. The reverse implication is immediate. Finite-color compactness also equates the finite and arbitrary-graph formulations. The full equivalence is proved as ReedReview.exactSpecial_iff_finiteSource in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean.

review.notes:
All three declarations and their invariant definitions were checked. The equivalence proofs compile without sorry dependencies; their axioms are only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Boundary checks cover empty graphs, singleton graphs, edgeless infinite graphs, and complete graphs. K₁,₆ was verified to satisfy the special-case hypotheses. An exhaustive computable test, proved equivalent to the finite inequality, passed for all 1,100 labeled simple graphs on zero through five vertices (/workspace/review/finite_tests.lean).

The Wiley full text was inaccessible (HTTP 403); only the original paper's abstract and metadata were retrieved. The mathematical statements were settled against the explicit formulations in the other two cited sources, including their remarks. Those pages do not record a resolution. The target file matches the committed version.
